CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

**The Role:**

We're hiring one of the first software engineers on our electro-optical team. Today that means long-range EO/IR sensors. In future it could mean sensors on mobile and airborne platforms. Wherever the sensor sits, the job is the software that makes it, and every sensor around it, act as one system.

This is a software engineering role first. You don't need to be a camera or computer vision specialist. You do need to be an excellent engineer who is curious about physical systems and understands how real sensors behave: they drift, they disagree with each other, and a field test doesn't care what the simulation said.

You'll join a small, elite team that takes its own work into the field. You'll test live, change code live, and see how it holds up on the next flight. The capabilities you build will push the frontier of what these systems can do, and few engineers anywhere get to work this close to the hardware, the mission and the result.

We're also changing how we build software. The aim is to take a feature or a new capability and develop as much of it as possible without real hardware, then push it up the chain: through simulation, through hardware in the loop, and on to full end-to-end tests in the real world. Simulation will keep improving, but real hardware will always have the final say. So we're building the harnesses and graphs that carry a capability through every one of those stages, with AI doing as much of the work as it can be trusted with. The end state is fully autonomous, end-to-end tests run against real hardware at our test sites. This is what you'll be building.

**What You'll Build:**

* Software that works on any sensor. Code that stays generic across many different camera heads and configurations while still hitting its performance bar, and flexes to whatever the mission and the customer demand.
* The path from desk to field. Harnesses and graphs that take a capability from first commit through simulation and hardware in the loop to a full end-to-end test, with as little manual effort as possible.
* Autonomous field testing. The system that runs complete tests against real hardware at our test sites on its own, and reports back what happened.
* Better simulation and replay. So more of every feature can be built and proven before it touches hardware.
* Multi-sensor integration. The interfaces, timing and data flow that let radar, cameras and other sensors work as one system.
* Fielded software. Deployment, monitoring and live fixes for systems running on edge hardware at test and customer sites.

  

**This Role Is Not:**

* Algorithm research. You'll build and ship software, not invent new detection or tracking algorithms.
* Physics modeling. You won't be building high-fidelity physics models in MATLAB or Simulink.
* Applied machine learning. You won't be training models on sensor data.
* Pure DevOps. You'll run infrastructure, but most of your time goes into writing software other engineers depend on.

  

**What We're Looking For:**

We care more about strong engineering fundamentals and curiosity than about any specific technology or domain.

* 3+ years of professional software engineering, including owning a production system end to end: you designed it, shipped it, and fixed it when it broke.
* A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Strong Python. You build services and tools other engineers depend on, not just scripts and notebooks.
* Comfort with Linux, Docker, networking and CI. You can get a multi-service system running on hardware you've never touched before.
* Real leverage from AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, with a considered view on what to delegate to them and what not to. We treat them as a multiplier on skills you already have: you should be able to write, explain and debug your own code without them.
* Grounding in the physical world, whether from an engineering degree, hands-on work with hardware, sensors or robotics, or field time with systems that had to work outside the lab. You can read a schematic, understand a test rack, and talk to an optics or RF engineer.
* An appetite for field work. You want to be on site when your code runs, and you can debug and ship a fix before the next flight.
* A habit of measuring rather than guessing: you build the experiment, then trust the data.

**Nice to Have:**

* Cameras, EO/IR sensors, gimbals, radar, or video pipelines such as GStreamer or DeepStream.
* Embedded Linux or edge computing, especially NVIDIA Jetson, and GPU or CUDA work.
* Robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones or aerospace.

* Building AI agent harnesses or workflow graphs.

* Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

jobs.description:
### **Description**

Impulse Space is seeking a **Embedded Linux Software Engineer** to develop and maintain the foundational software stack that powers our avionics platforms. This role requires deep expertise in embedded Linux, low-level hardware/software integration, and platform engineering practices to ensure secure, reliable, and maintainable systems.

### **Responsibilities**

  

* **Linux Distribution Development:**
  + Build, configure, and maintain a Yocto-based Linux distribution for custom avionics hardware.
  + Manage kernel configuration, system services, and integration of middleware components.
* **Board Bring-Up & Hardware Integration:**
  + Perform initial board bring-up of avionics computers.
  + Debug hardware/software integration issues across CPU, memory, and peripheral subsystems.
* **Driver Development & Debugging:**
  + Develop, port, and maintain Linux device drivers for sensors, communication buses, and memory devices.
  + Debug kernel-space and user-space interactions using hardware debuggers and tracing tools.
* **Platform Engineering & System Hardening:**
  + Implement secure boot and code signing for flight-critical binaries.
  + Configure and manage router certificates and other cryptographic assets.
  + Apply Linux security frameworks such as AppArmor and SELinux for mandatory access control.
  + Design and maintain OTA update infrastructure with rollback/A-B partitioning support.
  + Manage system configuration, startup scripts, and fault-tolerant resource allocation.

  

### **Minimum Qualifications**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degrees.
* Experience building and maintaining Yocto-based embedded Linux distributions for custom boards.
* Demonstrated ability to develop, configure, and debug Linux kernel drivers.
* Demonstrated experience developing in C/C++, with ability to work in constrained, low-level environments.

### **Preferred Skills and Experience**

  

* Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation, design reviews, and cross-discipline collaboration.
* Experience with UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, and similar buses.
* Strong understanding of embedded software principles, real-time constraints, and resource-limited systems.
* Experience with OTA update design and deployment (e.g., dual-partition or rollback-safe systems).
* Familiarity with system hardening and security frameworks (SELinux, AppArmor, secure boot, TPM/cryptographic key management).
* Experience with CI/CD pipelines for embedded systems (e.g., GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI).
* Familiarity with containerization and reproducible build techniques for embedded platforms.
* Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, hardware debuggers, and signal analyzers.

At Luna, you will work with some of the most curious, forward-thinking engineers and scientists in the industry to shape the future of fiber optic measurement.

**Role Overview**

We are seeking a Software Engineer II, with flexibility to hire at the Senior level for the right candidate, to join the software development team for our photonics instrumentation. Final level and pay will be based on experience, skills, and qualifications. You will build the applications that control precision optical instruments, process high-speed measurement data, and visualize complex optical behavior in real time. You will develop software for Linux and Windows platforms, including embedded Linux devices, and support the remote control interfaces customers use to integrate our instruments into their own test systems.

If you are passionate about hardware-software integration and want to build the software behind state-of-the-art optical test equipment, we want you on our team.

* **Application Development:** Design, develop, and maintain reliable C/C++ and Python applications for Linux and Windows, including user-facing applications and GUIs.

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

**Role**

Northwood engineers and operators run hardware and software across a global network of antenna ground stations and the cloud services behind them. No one sells a platform for running a network like this at scale, so Northwood builds its own.

Platform Engineering builds the software that takes Northwood products from first prototype to full operation. That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. Every one of these problems has to work across every site, service, and customer at once.

Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow.

As an early-career Software Engineer on the Platform team, you'll ship to real production systems from your first weeks, with close mentorship, and take on more ownership as you show you're ready. You don't need to know every part of the stack today. You need to learn fast, reason clearly through problems you haven't seen before, and care a lot about what you build.

  + Build simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, so every release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site.

  + Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, and updated, in remote locations with few or no people on site.

**The Role:**

We're hiring one of the first software engineers on our electro-optical team. Today that means long-range EO/IR sensors. In future it could mean sensors on mobile and airborne platforms. Wherever the sensor sits, the job is the software that makes it, and every sensor around it, act as one system.

This is a software engineering role first. You don't need to be a camera or computer vision specialist. You do need to be an excellent engineer who is curious about physical systems and understands how real sensors behave: they drift, they disagree with each other, and a field test doesn't care what the simulation said.

You'll join a small, elite team that takes its own work into the field. You'll test live, change code live, and see how it holds up on the next flight. The capabilities you build will push the frontier of what these systems can do, and few engineers anywhere get to work this close to the hardware, the mission and the result.

We're also changing how we build software. The aim is to take a feature or a new capability and develop as much of it as possible without real hardware, then push it up the chain: through simulation, through hardware in the loop, and on to full end-to-end tests in the real world. Simulation will keep improving, but real hardware will always have the final say. So we're building the harnesses and graphs that carry a capability through every one of those stages, with AI doing as much of the work as it can be trusted with. The end state is fully autonomous, end-to-end tests run against real hardware at our test sites. This is what you'll be building.

**What You'll Build:**

* Autonomous field testing. The system that runs complete tests against real hardware at our test sites on its own, and reports back what happened.
* Better simulation and replay. So more of every feature can be built and proven before it touches hardware.
* Multi-sensor integration. The interfaces, timing and data flow that let radar, cameras and other sensors work as one system.
* Fielded software. Deployment, monitoring and live fixes for systems running on edge hardware at test and customer sites.

  

**This Role Is Not:**

* Algorithm research. You'll build and ship software, not invent new detection or tracking algorithms.
* Physics modeling. You won't be building high-fidelity physics models in MATLAB or Simulink.
* Applied machine learning. You won't be training models on sensor data.
* Pure DevOps. You'll run infrastructure, but most of your time goes into writing software other engineers depend on.

We care more about strong engineering fundamentals and curiosity than about any specific technology or domain.

* 3+ years of professional software engineering, including owning a production system end to end: you designed it, shipped it, and fixed it when it broke.
* A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or a related field, or equivalent experience.
